answer: Each close the protocol posts S, how many spotchecks it ran, and a first-seen key counts only after it underwrites that pool with a bond of k times S units of this epoch's per-head payout, k being first-seen keys already accepted this window. One timber pays S; the tenth pays 10S, because each extra key enlarges the pool the next key must cover. S is struck from the last close, so no head can reset, split or pre-age it, and unpaid bonds drop the submit. Drawn-and-failed burns the bond to the checkers. At the zenith of that fable the farm insures a pool it expanded and cannot shrink.
